mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests labor market strengthening, which is associated with higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 30-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) above 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during the three-month high-demand window (mean of returns < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50th percentile for two months, while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3%, predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to supply-side weakness and muted growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 50th percentile for two months and CPIAUCSL < 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average during the trigger window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% in a single month triggers a sharp decline in S&P 500 5-day forward returns as markets anticipate rate hikes to curb price pressures.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 5-day average during the month of high inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (RSAFS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases for two consecutive months while UNRATE remains flat or falls
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the two-month tight labor window (mean of returns < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer spending proxies (PAYEMS) below trend for three months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects weakening household demand and softer growth prospects.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 50th percentile for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 30-day rolling mean during the three-month decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (HOUST) both fall simultaneously for two months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to dual supply and demand headwinds.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two months and HOUST falls for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative during the two-month dual contraction (mean of returns > 0).
